capability.name: Managing policy definitions
capability.purpose: Load, download and inspect the policy definition files (ADMX/ADML) and the products and support rules they declare.

layers.name: Screens
layers.purpose: What a person sees and enters: Windows Forms windows and dialogs, their layout, the handlers that react to a person using them, and the small value shapes dialogs fill in and hand back to the main window.

actions.name: Options_CheckedChanged
actions.purpose: Enables the folder box and Browse button only when the custom folder option is chosen.

context.scope: Action started by a person in the OpenAdmxFolder screen of Managing policy definitions: Enables the folder box and Browse button only when the custom folder option is chosen.
rules: In the Open ADMX folder dialog the folder text box and Browse button are usable only while the custom folder choice is selected. (PolicyPlus/OpenAdmxFolder.vb:7)
unconfirmed: For the capability: When several sibling language folders share the chosen language, such as de-AT and de-CH for de-DE, the one used depends on the order Windows lists folders. The code states no preference among them. If wrong: People may see definitions in a different regional variant of their language than expected.

For the capability: When linking stops the load with an error, what the person sees depends on the calling screen, which reports a failed load but whose exact message and the state left in the workspace we did not trace. If wrong: A person might see a different message, or be left with a partly loaded set of definitions.

For the capability: The download assumes Microsoft still serves the fixed Windows 11 26H2 package at its link, with definitions at the expected folder inside it. If not, the download fails with a step message. If wrong: Downloads fail at the download or move step, and the person cannot fetch definitions from within the program.

For the capability: Offering the domain definitions folder relies on Windows reporting the computer's domain. When Windows cannot, the choice is silently disabled, so domain-joined machines without reachable controllers cannot pick it. If wrong: The domain choice could appear or stay disabled differently than described.

concerns.name: Reading and writing policy values in policy files and the registry
concerns.purpose: Every policy lookup and change goes through one store of keys and values, held in a policy file or the live registry. Browsing, setting, raw editing and loading all lean on it, as does definition management.

concerns.name: Looking up display text from definition strings
concerns.purpose: Policy names and descriptions are written as string codes in the definition files. This turns a code into text for the language loaded, and every screen showing policy text relies on it.

concerns.name: Enabling Windows privileges for protected files and hives
concerns.purpose: Before loading user policy hives or replacing protected definition files, the program asks Windows for backup, restore or ownership rights. Loading policy sources, policy setting and definition download lean on it.

concerns.name: Checking whether this Windows edition has Group Policy
concerns.purpose: Tells the program whether the machine's Windows edition includes the Group Policy machinery, so it can adapt what it offers. Start-up and policy source loading use it.
